SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-10: FHIRPath — §5.6.6-§5.6.12 String Manipulation (Transform). Test these items: upper(), lower(), replace(pattern, substitution), matches(regex), replaceMatches(regex, substitution), length(), toChars(). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.6.9 matches(regex : String) and §5.6.10 replaceMatches(regex : String, substitution : String)
issues.evidence: Fresh FP-10 HISTORIAN probe: `s.matches('[invalid')` is a malformed regex. Native public result UDFs return empty/NULL but `fhirpath_is_valid` returns true; forced Python fallback raises a DuckDB InvalidInputException from `re.compile` instead of row-resilient empty/NULL and false validity.
issues.root_cause: Native validateFHIRPathRegex only enforced length/ReDoS guards and did not compile the regex before empty-input short-circuiting; Python fallback let re.error escape from cached regex compilation instead of converting it to FHIRPathError; fallback literal-regex validity precheck called only the guard helper, not compilation.
issues.resolution: Native regex validation now compiles the normalized pattern and raises FHIRPathSpecError for malformed syntax. Python _compile_regex wraps re.error in FHIRPathError, and fhirpath_is_valid() uses _compile_regex for literal regex arguments.
issues.verified_in: Fresh FP-10 HISTORIAN probe 51/51; pytest test_string_transform_parity.py 4 passed; native fhirpath sqllogictest 470 assertions; full conformance 2822/2822.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.6.6 upper() : String and §5.6.7 lower() : String
issues.evidence: Fresh FP-10 HISTORIAN probe: native C++ `latin_ext_lower.upper()` over `čžš` returns `Čžš` while fallback/spec expectation is `ČŽŠ`; native `latin_ext.lower()` over `ČŽŠ` returns `čŽŠ` while fallback/spec expectation is `čžš`.
issues.root_cause: Native Unicode case conversion covered ASCII, Latin-1, early Latin Extended-A pairs, Greek, and Cyrillic but missed later common Latin Extended-A alternating case ranges such as Š/š and Ž/ž.
issues.resolution: Extended native upper/lower case mapping for the remaining common Latin Extended-A pair ranges, including č/Č, ž/Ž, and š/Š.
issues.verified_in: Fresh FP-10 HISTORIAN probe 51/51; pytest test_string_transform_parity.py 4 passed; native fhirpath sqllogictest 470 assertions; full conformance 2822/2822.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.6.8 replace(pattern : String, substitution : String) : String
issues.evidence: Fresh FP-10 HISTORIAN probe: `empty.replace('z','x')` where `empty` is a singleton empty string returns `['']` in native C++ but empty collection in forced Python fallback. The spec's empty-propagation rule applies to empty collections/arguments, not to a present empty string with a non-matching pattern.
issues.root_cause: Python fallback replace() used a truthiness check on the input string and returned empty collection for an empty string value, conflating a singleton empty String with an empty input collection.
issues.resolution: Removed the input-string truthiness shortcut so a present empty String follows ordinary string replacement semantics and returns the original empty string when a non-empty pattern is not found.
issues.verified_in: Fresh FP-10 HISTORIAN probe 51/51; pytest test_string_transform_parity.py 4 passed; native fhirpath sqllogictest 470 assertions; full conformance 2822/2822.
